## Findings by module

### 6

- **extended** (debt speech 29/07/1987): Sankara's OAU speech (a modified English translation by Viewpoint Magazine, CC BY-NC) argues the debt cannot be repaid: its origins lie in colonialism, lenders are the former colonisers, debt is 'neo-colonialism' and a 'reconquest', Africa owes a 'blood debt' for the world wars, and Africa should form an 'Addis Ababa Club' united front against debt, cut arms purchases and 'produce in Africa, consume in Africa'. He cites Brundtland, Castro, Mitterrand and Houphouet-Boigny as saying poor states cannot repay. He says Burkina Faso alone would be punished, 'I will not be here for the next conference' (he was killed on 15/10/1987, per the course). Use as a primary voice in Module 6 beside Moyo (who argues for market borrowing) and Rodney (dependency); it states an aim and a claim, not a result. Several claims are rhetoric (for example that debt is simply 'colonisers' lending to themselves').

### 4

- **confirmed** (speech and record): The course's statement that Sankara spoke against debt at the OAU in 1987 is confirmed by the primary text (Addis Ababa summit, 29/07/1987). The text contains none of the course's other Sankara claims (vaccination figures, tribunals, unions), so those remain from the library. He also proposes sanctions on heads of state who skip African summits, and says all would gain from disarmament.
